newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate ends unchanged at 5.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate ends unchanged at 5.5 pct.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate remained unchanged at 5.5/8 percent as the market remained thin and wary of central bank's presence as lender, money dealers said on Tuesday.
They said some big banks were still lending, possibly to help in Bank Negara's efforts to keep interest rates down.
Earlier, interbank rates were mostly unchanged in the morning as liquidity remained ample and demand low.
One-month money was at 7.40/50 percent, three-month money was at 7.50/60 percent and one-week rate was at 6.00/40 percent.

Bank Negara has been keeping interest rates under check through injection of funds, after an abandoned defense of the ringgit through intervention drained six to eight billion ringgit from the system.
It also imposed restrictions on local banks to limit their swap transactions to $2.0 million per overseas customer.
Interest rate futures ended lower in extremely thin trading as a perception gained ground that Bank Negara will not be able to hold down interbank rates for too long, futures dealers said.
"There is no indication that there will be any long-term policy measure to keep interest rates down," said a futures dealer with a Malaysian bank.
"This way (through funds injection) they can hold rates down only for a short time," he said.
The three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down three points to 92.42, or an implied yield of 7.62 percent.
The December contract was also down three at 92.58, or 7.42 percent and March 1998 fell three to 92.63, or 7.37 percent.
